question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Like a bat out of hell
solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"Like a bat out of hell"** means to move very fast and wildly. (बहुत तेज और बेकाबू तरीके से)

 
 
• **Example:** He ran out of the room like a bat out of hell when he heard the fire alarm.
 
 
 
• **Very fast and wildly** indicates a rapid and uncontrolled manner. (बहुत तेज और बेकाबू तरीके से)
 
 
• **Example:** The motorcycle sped down the highway very fast and wildly.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings:

 
• **In a bad situation** (खराब स्थिति में): Facing or experiencing difficulties.

 
 
• **Example:** He found himself in a bad situation after losing his job.
 
 
 
• **Defeated** (पराजित): Having been beaten in a battle or other contest.
 
 
• **Example:** The team felt defeated after losing the final match.
 
 
 
• **Impossible** (असंभव): Not able to occur, exist, or be done.
 
 
• **Example:** It seems impossible to complete this project within the deadline.
